results.ask: My flux-cored welds have porosity. What should I check?
results.text:
For flux-cored (gasless, DCEN) porosity, check these — from the wire weld porosity causes list [p.37]:

**1. Polarity** — this is the most common culprit for flux-cored. It must be set to DCEN: Wire Feed Power Cable in the Negative (–) socket, Ground Clamp Cable in the Positive (+) socket [p.13, p.37]. If someone left it wired for MIG (DCEP), that alone will cause porosity.

**2. Dirty workpiece or wire** — clean the workpiece down to bare metal, and make sure the wire is free of oil, rust, or coatings [p.37].

**3. Inconsistent travel speed** — keep a steady, even pace along the joint [p.37].

**4. CTWD (contact tip to work distance) too long** — keep it short; the manual specifies keeping it at 1/2" or less generally for these wire processes [p.36, p.37].

Note: the shielding-gas causes on that same list (flow too low/high, wrong gas) don't apply to you — flux-cored is gasless [p.18].If you want to double check your cable setup against the diagram itself, the DCEN flux-cored polarity page is [p.13].
